title: Gradient-based admission controller and kernel diversification for tail-latency reduction
creator: Priya Raman
description: Introduce a gradient-driven admission controller that observes short-window latency and queue gradients to make admission decisions, paired with a kernel diversification layer that dynamically selects between optimized FP16, int8, and trimmed-attention kernels. The goal is to reduce 95/99th tail latency for mixed-prefill/decode workloads while preserving throughput and minimizing unit cost.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile latency for representative chat workload decreases by >= 20% under realistic burst traces compared to baseline
99th percentile latency improves by >= 10% without dropping >2% throughput at 95% CPU/GPU utilization
No more than 1% increase in per-token cost on average for non-degraded SLO traffic; configurable knob to prioritize latency vs cost
Kernel selection decisions are explainable in the debug trace and present in Console per-request routing metadata
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rollout via console canary control
implementation_notes: Add a small in-memory sliding window to each admission node that computes latency gradient and variance over last 1s, 5s buckets
Admission decision = sigmoid(w1*latency_grad + w2*queue_len_ratio + w3*prefill_rate_change) with tunable weights per tenant

Kernel Diversification module wraps current kernel selection: consult model-profile (seq-dist, memory budget) -> simulate estimated token-ms for candidate kernels -> pick kernel with lowest tail-cost metric
Introduce a lightweight sampler that probes alternate kernels on a small fraction of requests (0.5%) to update cost model continuously
Prefetch and attention prewarm: use trace-based attention hinting for long-prefix requests, pre-allocate KV cache lanes and tag request with hint TTL
Scheduling: implement slot-annealing that allows micro-slices of earlier-prefilled requests to be advanced when gradients indicate impending tail spike
Observability: emit events kernel_choice, admission_score, probe_result to tracing and console dashboard
progress_updates: 2026-02-22 - Kickoff meeting. Agreed success metrics and bench traces (customer-chat-burst, docs-indexing). Priya to land design doc; Marco to prototype admission sigmoid in simulator.
2026-02-28 - Simulator prototype shows admission gradient reduces peak queue length by ~18% on synthetic microburst trace. Identified unstable weight combos; added L2 penalty and weight clamping.

2026-03-04 - Kernel diversification spec refined: include estimated KV-cache pressure and decode CPU time in cost model. Decided to avoid switching kernels mid-decode for safety; only switch at request boundary or when prefill is complete.

2026-03-09 - End-to-end smoke run in staging with 0.5% kernel probe enabled. Observed one repro of increased 99th latency due to probe selecting a slower kernel for long-seq requests. Mitigation: add sequence-length threshold to probe eligibility and conservative fallback after probe failures.
